newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 29.

text.p: These are some leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin criticised some officials for lack of caution when talking about Hong Kong. He urged all government officials to take care with their words on Hong Kong and follow the policies of the central government.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY -- A total 31 candidates have registered to run for Chief Executive of the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR).
-- APPLE DAILY -- Chinese leaders have not decided who they want for Hong Kong Chief Executive and have told government departments to keep a distance from the four frontrunners.
-- SING TAO -- Chief Executive candidate Simon Li revealed confidential information of next year's transitional budget, when economic growth was estimated to be 4.75 per cent.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Guangdong province is cracking down on illegally imported Hong Kong newspapers. Readers have been encouraged by the horseracing pages. According to present rules, only four pro-Beijing papers from Hong Kong are allowed to be sold in China.
-- Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese Premier Li Peng said China would send senior leaders to participate in the handover ceremony in Hong Kong next year.
-- The jobless rate in Chinese cities and towns has risen by three percent in the past three quarters. The number of registered jobless people hit 5.5 million by end September.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Hong Kong's Industrial Support Plan has allocated $700 million funds for 81 projects in the past three years and would review the plan in November.

-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A consortium controlled by local tycoon Li Ka-shing and the family of Chief Executive hopeful Tung Chee-hwa were under pressure from Chinese officials to further reduce its majority stake in the US$1.5 billion Oriental Plaza project in Beijing.
-- The first voice-recognition software tuned to Cantonese will be demonstrated in Hong Kong by Apple Computer this week.
-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- Promotions for expatriate civil servants will be held up for two months to avoid newly-promoted officers quitting due to the handover.
-- Hong Kong Monetary Authority chief Joseph Yam warned against withdrawal of investments by Asian central banks in European currencies after European Monetary Union in 1999.
